companies.subsequent_events: Jul 28, 2026: wholly-owned subsidiary Galaxy Helios Data Centers II LLC closed $3.507B 9.875% Senior Secured Notes due Aug 1, 2031 (priced ~Jul 23-24; ISIN US36322DAA46); interest Feb 1/Aug 1 from Feb 1, 2027; 4%/yr amortization of original principal starting >=10 months after project completion; first-priority liens on substantially all issuer/guarantor assets plus pledge of parent's equity in issuer; proceeds fund two Helios Phase II buildings and debt-service reserves. Reported as project-level, not recourse to Galaxy parent. No agency rating found. Pro forma gross debt ~$6.95B (derived: $3,447.5M + $3,507M), of which ~$4.8B project-level. 3.00% 2026 exchangeables ($445M) mature Dec 15, 2026 - no repayment/exchange disclosure found as of Oct 9.
companies.covenants_and_key_terms: Helios II notes: first-lien on project assets and parent equity pledge, debt-service reserve, scheduled 4% annual amortization post-completion, high coupon reflects non-IG tenant (CoreWeave). DB Helios I term loan: senior secured, up to $1.4B, commitments to Aug 15, 2028. Exchangeables: GDH LP senior unsecured, exchangeable into Class A shares.
companies.credit_view: Galaxy is two credits: a volatile, mark-to-market trading/treasury business with ~$2.5B cash+stablecoins and ~$1.2B net digital assets funded partly by $2.15B low-coupon exchangeables, and a ring-fenced Helios data-center platform financed with project debt against a 526 MW CoreWeave lease (~$10.4B min payments). Corporate leverage on consolidated EBITDA is meaningless (adj EBITDA negative for three straight quarters on crypto marks), so the corporate credit rests on liquidity and asset coverage, which is ample versus the $445M Dec-2026 maturity. Helios debt (~$1.3B DB loan + $3.5B 9.875% notes) is a single-tenant, construction-stage exposure to a non-IG counterparty; Phase I (~$80M/qtr revenue, >90% margin) is now cash-generating. Key risks: Phase II construction/completion, CoreWeave credit, crypto drawdowns hitting the parent's liquidity cushion.

companies.credit_view: Riot's recourse balance sheet is light: $594.4M of 0.75% 2030 converts against $471M unrestricted cash and ~11,380 BTC (~$0.9B at ~$82K), so it is net cash including BTC, and the Coinbase line has been repaid. The credit story has shifted to the 191 MW frontier-AI-lab lease (~$9.1B over 20 years), a high-quality tenant but with $1.7-2.1B of project debt still to be placed. The near-term risk is the $573M Morgan Stanley bridge maturing Dec 31, 2026, a year before rent begins; failure to land the IG-backed permanent financing would push Riot to fund with BTC sales or equity. Mining EBITDA is negative/volatile and adj EBITDA is distorted by BTC marks.

companies.credit_view: MARA's credit is a bitcoin-collateral story: ~$2.3B of mostly zero-coupon converts (no material maturity until Mar 2030) are covered by ~35.6K BTC (~$2.9B at ~$82K) and $421M cash, so it is roughly net-cash including BTC, but mining EBITDA is negative and adjusted EBITDA swings with BTC marks. Management has shown willingness to sell BTC to buy back converts at a discount (~$1.0B retired in March 2026 at ~91% of par), which supports creditors. The pivot to secured BTC-backed loans ($750M, 18,750 BTC pledged) and a pending $1.5B Long Ridge purchase with an up-to-$785M bridge subordinates converts structurally and raises margin-call risk in a BTC drawdown. Credit hinges on BTC price, execution of the Long Ridge/AI conversion, and term-out of the bridge.
